procedural_history.impugned_order: Order of the learned Single Judge of the High Court of Judicature at Bombay in Criminal Appeal No.298 of 2024, which upheld the Special Judge's rejection of the appellant's bail application.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The appellant filed a criminal appeal (No. 298 of 2024) in the High Court of Judicature at Bombay challenging the Special Judge's order rejecting his bail application. The High Court, in a well-reasoned order, rejected the appeal and upheld the denial of bail.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellant approached the Supreme Court challenging the High Court's order. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, quashing the orders of both the Special Court and the High Court.

decision.conviction_status: The order passed by the Special Court dated 02.02.2024 and the impugned order of the learned Single Judge dated 29.07.2024 are quashed and set aside.
directions: The appellant is directed to be released on bail

issue.issue_text: Whether the appeal challenging the order of the Special Court dated 02.02.2024 and the impugned order of the learned Single Judge dated 29.07.2024 should be allowed.

facts: The case is an appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 5438 of 2024) challenging an order from a Single Judge of the High Court of Judicature at Bombay.
The High Court's order (dated 29.07.2024) had rejected the appellant's appeal.
The appellant's initial appeal to the High Court was against an order from a Special Court (dated 02.02.2024) which had rejected the appellant's bail application.
The State and the complainant vehemently opposed the appeal in the Supreme Court.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court decided to allow the appeal. It explicitly stated, "We are, therefore, inclined to allow the appeal." As a result, the Court quashed and set aside both the order of the Special Court dated 02.02.2024 and the order of the learned Single Judge dated 29.07.2024. The final outcome is summarized in the text as "Result of the case: Appeal allowed."

arguments.issue_text: Whether the appeal challenging the order of the Special Court dated 02.02.2024 and the impugned order of the learned Single Judge dated 29.07.2024 should be allowed.
appellant_arguments: The appellant relied on the case of Javed Gulam Nabi Shaikh v. State of Maharashtra and Another.
respondent_arguments: The learned Single Judge of the High Court had already rejected the appellant's appeal with an elaborate and well-reasoned order.
The appellant is part of a gang that has caused terror in the area and is indulging in criminal activities.
The learned Single Judge rightly rejected the appellant's reliance on the case of Javed Gulam Nabi Shaikh v. State of Maharashtra and Another.
No interference is warranted in the present appeal.

cases.case_name: State of Maharashtra v. Vishwnath Maranna Shetty
cases.principle: The Supreme Court found no error in the reasoning of the lower court (Single Judge), which had relied on this judgment to reject the appellant's appeal.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: No binding legal rule can be extracted, as the provided text contains a final decision that allows the appeal and quashes the lower court's order, while simultaneously including statements that find no error in the lower court's reasoning.
obiter: We, therefore, find no error in the reasoning adopted by the learned Single Judge, inasmuch as the learned Single Judge has relied on the judgment of this Court in the case of State of Maharashtra v. Vishwnath Maranna Shetty.
At the outset, we may state that the learned Single Judge by an elaborate and well reasoned order rejected the appeal of the appellant herein.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court's reasoning is internally contradictory. It explicitly states that the learned Single Judge's order rejecting the appellant's appeal was "elaborate and well reasoned" and that the court finds "no error in the reasoning adopted by the learned Single Judge." Despite this endorsement of the lower court's logic for denying bail, the Supreme Court immediately concludes, without providing any counter-reasoning, that it is "inclined to allow the appeal" and quash the very orders it found no error with.
legal_tests_applied: The court referenced the legal test applied by the lower court, which required the satisfaction of twin conditions for bail under the relevant Act: (i) Satisfaction of the Court that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the accused is not guilty of the alleged offence; and (ii) He/she is not likely to commit any offence while on bail.
why_respondent_won: The learned Single Judge by an elaborate and well reasoned order rejected the appeal of the appellant herein.

We, therefore, find no error in the reasoning adopted by the learned Single Judge, inasmuch as the learned Single Judge has relied on the judgment of this Court in the case of State of Maharashtra v. Vishwnath Maranna Shetty.

A perusal of the judgment of the learned Single Judge would reveal that the learned Judge has basically rejected the appeal on the ground that the twin conditions as required under the provisions of the said Act i.e. (i) Satisfaction of the Court that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the accused is not guilty of the alleged offence; and (ii) He/she is not likely to commit any offence while on bail. While doing so, the learned Judge has given elaborate reasonings and has held that the appellant is not entitled to grant of bail.
policy_considerations: In order to protect the interest of the prosecution as well as the victim, we are inclined to impose certain stringent conditions on the appellant.
